title: Implementing small size variant for ActionList.Item
body: Closes #8008 Adds a `small` size variant to `ActionList.Item` and `ActionList.LinkItem`. The new variant uses small body text and compact block padding, providing a supported alternative to consumer-side CSS overrides for dense interfaces. The PR also adds Storybook coverage, updates the generated API documentation and playground controls, and extends the existing size prop test coverage. As stated in the issue this PR is closing, this would address the current hack around the new PR Overview sidebar. I specifically would like to do the same on a different sidebar, Alerts (Dependabot, Code Scanning and Secret Scanning). All three are currently using the default "medium" size and it would look better if it was smaller. [Storybook](https://ui.githubapp.com/storybook/?path=/story/apps-dependabot-alertshowsidebar--all-tags) ### Changelog #### New - Added `size="small"` support to `ActionList.Item` and `ActionList.LinkItem`. - Added a Storybook example covering labels with inline and block descriptions. #### Changed - Updated the `size` prop type and documentation to include `small`. - Updated Storybook playground controls to expose the new size. - Expanded tests to verify small sizing on both item variants. #### Removed - None. ### Rollout strategy - [x] No changes needed in github/github-ui - [ ] Needs changes in github/github-ui - [ ] Ships with feature flag(s) - [ ] Not sure - [ ] None This is an additive, opt-in API change. Existing items continue to default to `medium`. ### Testing & Reviewing - Review the `SmallItem` Storybook story, including inline and block descriptions. - Verify `size="small"` applies compact block padding and small body typography. - Verify `medium`, `large`, and the default `medium` behavior remain unchanged. - CI includes React 18 and React 19 tests, type checks, linting, formatting, and visual/accessibility test coverage.

title: fix(Button): apply disabled styles while loading under FF
body:
Related #7879

Loading primary buttons already set `aria-disabled` and drop `onClick`, but CSS skipped disabled visuals whenever `data-loading` was true. Native `disabled` was the only way to get the muted primary look, which is inaccessible for form submit buttons.

This adds an opt-in way to apply the existing `aria-disabled` styles to loading buttons. Behind the `primer_react_button_loading_disabled_styles` feature flag, `<Button variant="primary" loading>` now looks like a disabled primary button, stays focusable, and does not use native `disabled`. The flag defaults to `false`, so existing loading-button visuals are unchanged until an app opts in.

### Changelog

#### New

- New feature flag `primer_react_button_loading_disabled_styles` (default `false`). When enabled, loading `Button`, `IconButton`, and `LinkButton` render a new `data-loading-disabled-styles` attribute and pick up disabled visuals while remaining keyboard-focusable.

#### Changed

- `ButtonBase.module.css` now has an additional `[aria-disabled='true'][data-loading-disabled-styles='true']` selector alongside the existing `[aria-disabled='true']:not([data-loading='true'])` selector, so the old always-on loading styles are preserved when the flag is off.

#### Removed

### Rollout strategy

- [x] Patch release
- [ ] Minor release
- [ ] Major release; if selected, include a written rollout or migration plan
- [ ] None; if selected, include a brief description as to why
- [x] Ships with feature flag(s): `primer_react_button_loading_disabled_styles` (default off)

This is an opt-in visual change gated behind a feature flag, so there is no behavior change for consumers who don't enable it.

### Testing & Reviewing

- Compare `Loading`, `Disabled`, and `Primary` in Storybook with the `primer_react_button_loading_disabled_styles` feature flag toggled on via the beaker icon in the toolbar (flag is off by default, so the dropdown toggle is required to see the new visuals)
- Unit tests assert loading primary matches disabled primary styles without the `disabled` attribute when the flag is enabled, and that loading styles are unchanged when it is disabled
- Loading buttons remain focusable and do not fire `onClick`, regardless of the flag
- `inactive` primary styling is unchanged

title: Truncate: infer props from `as` and forward `inline` to custom `as` components
body:
`<Truncate as={Link} href={url} title={url} maxWidth={600} inline>` never gave `Link` its `inline` prop. Truncate used `inline` for its own styling and did not pass it on, so `Link`'s inline behaviour (underlines inside text) never turned on.

```tsx
<Truncate as={Link} href={url} title={url} maxWidth={600} inline muted>
  {url}
</Truncate>
```

### Changelog

#### New

- Type tests in `Truncate.types.test.tsx` for props inferred from `as`:
  - intrinsic elements (`as="a"` accepts `href`, `as="div"` rejects it)
  - components (`as={Link}` accepts `muted` and rejects unknown props)
  - `title` still required
  - typed event handlers

#### Changed

- `Truncate` passes `inline` to the `as` component when that component is a React component. It is still left off plain HTML tags such as `'span'`, so no invalid `inline` attribute reaches the DOM.
- `Truncate` now uses `PolymorphicProps` + `fixedForwardRef` from `utils/modern-polymorphic`, the same typing as `Link`, `Text` and `BranchName`, replacing the older `ForwardRefComponent` typing.
- `TruncateProps` now takes the `as` type as a generic parameter, defaulting to `'div'`, so existing uses of `TruncateProps` still compile.

#### Removed

### Rollout strategy

- [ ] No changes needed in github/github-ui
- [x] Needs changes in github/github-ui
- [ ] Ships with feature flag(s)
- [ ] Not sure
- [ ] None

The typing change could still surface type errors in consumers passing props that don't match their `as` target, which a github-ui integration run would catch.

### Testing & Reviewing

- `maxWidth` and `expandable` are deliberately **not** passed on. They only drive Truncate's own CSS, and components like `Link` pass unknown props straight onto the DOM element. Passing them on makes React warn ("React does not recognize the `maxWidth` prop…"), which fails tests when console errors are enforced. `inline` is the one Truncate prop that `Link` also defines.
- For the runtime behaviour, see the new unit tests: `Link` gets `data-inline` from its own `inline` prop, a custom component receives `inline`, and `as="span"` gets no `inline` attribute.
- I haven't run a github-ui integration build for the typing change.

title: UnderlineNav: Avoid default # href for custom links
body:
Closes github/primer#6384

`UnderlineNav.Item` currently adds `href="#"` whenever `href` is omitted, including when an item renders through a custom component supplied with `as`. This can give router links both `to` and `href` props and interfere with soft navigation.

This change keeps the fallback for native anchors, omits `href` entirely for custom components unless the consumer supplies it, and updates the component documentation to describe that behavior.

### Changelog

- `UnderlineNav.Item` no longer adds a default `href` when rendered as a custom component.
- Native anchor items continue to default to `href="#"`.
